To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
relaxin is a mediator of reduced mesangial cell reactivity to Ang II during gestation.

(1) MCs from pregnant rats display refractoriness to the effects of Ang II on [Ca] i; (2) this refractoriness is mediated by RLX and is independent of NO and the AT2R; (3) RLX can be a therapeutic target for the management of renal disorders associated with the RAS.
the mesangial cells cultured from pregnant rats display reduced reactivity to angiotensin II and this response is mediated by relaxin and its receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the renin-angiotensin system, which is involved in several physiological and pathological conditions.
the mechanisms involved in the refractoriness to angiotensin II in the mesangial cells during pregnancy.
the mechanisms that underlie the refractoriness to the effects of Ang II on MCs in pregnant rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MCs from the pregnant rats are refractory to Ang II, and the mechanisms involved in this phenomenon include the up-regulation of RLX, RXFP1, AT2 and NO.

1) MCs from pregnant rats display a reduced reactivity to Ang II, compared to MCs from virgin rats; 2) RLX is involved in the refractoriness to the MCs of pregnant rats; 3) the RXFP1 receptor mediates this effect of RLX; 4) the AT2 receptor is not involved in this response; 5) NO synthase inhibitor does not affect the refractoriness.
RLX is involved in the refractoriness to the effects of Ang II in the mesangial cell during pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RLX is an important regulator of the RAS during pregnancy and may be a therapeutic target in preeclampsia.
the refractoriness observed in the MCs cultured from pregnant rats to the Ang II-induced increase in [Ca+]i is related to the increased production of relaxin and the activation of the RXFP1 receptor.
the AT2 receptor and NO are not involved in the response of MCs from P group to Ang II, but the RXFP1 receptor and RLX may be involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RLX can act as an important mediator of the refractory response to Ang II of MCs cultured from pregnant rats.
RLX is able to modulate the re-activity of the MC to Ang II, which could be important in the control of the GFR during pregnancy.
the refractoriness observed in the MCs from pregnant rats to Ang II is not due to the increased NO production or the AT2 receptor activation, but rather to the increase in RLX levels.
